provenance.notes: Ext family batch. Small niche that recurs by nature, so the kit leans on restain plans and seasonal timing. No stain brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: Deck stain colour and opacity guide
pageStructurePlus.contains: Clear, toner, semi-transparent, semi-solid and solid stains compared by look and wear, with colour samples on cedar, pine and pressure-treated boards
pageStructurePlus.why: Opacity decides how the deck looks and how soon it needs redoing. Buyers who understand it choose faster and complain less.

pageStructurePlus.section: Wash, strip and sand prep for decks
pageStructurePlus.contains: Cleaning, stripping old stain, wood brightener, sanding raised grain, drying time, and why peeling solid stain costs more to fix
pageStructurePlus.why: Prep is the difference between a stain that lasts and one that peels by next summer. It explains why quotes differ.

pageStructurePlus.section: New wood and composite deck care
pageStructurePlus.contains: When new pressure-treated or cedar decks can take stain, cleaning composite decks that shouldn't be stained, and mould on composite boards
pageStructurePlus.why: New deck owners ask when to stain, and composite owners ask what to do instead. Both are easy jobs if the page answers first.

pageStructurePlus.section: Board and railing repairs before staining
pageStructurePlus.contains: Popped nails and screws, loose railings, cracked or rotted boards, wobbly stairs, and replacing boards to match before the stain goes on
pageStructurePlus.why: Small repairs found on the walk-around lift the ticket. Listing them up front stops the quote feeling padded.

pageStructurePlus.section: Fence staining by the linear foot
pageStructurePlus.contains: One side or both, the neighbour's side and permission, spray versus brush, overspray protection for cars and plants, and gates
pageStructurePlus.why: Fence staining is priced and decided differently from decks. A page of its own catches fence searches and sets expectations.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Maintenance coats on a schedule by stain type, a yearly wash, reminders before the season, and plan sign-up
pageStructurePlus.why: Stain wears out on a cycle. A plan turns one deck into a customer for years and fills the spring calendar ahead of time.

openers.line: Your listing has deck staining reviews but no website button. Someone looking at a grey, splintery deck on a Sunday wants to see your before-and-afters and ask for a quote then.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: A deck staining page for that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your website link opens Facebook. A homeowner choosing between semi-transparent and solid deck stain wants a colour guide, and a feed buries it.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest deck or fence posted.
openers.linkLine: A deck stain colour guide instead of a feed: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your staining site still has a free-host banner and a broken quote form. When people plan to have the deck redone every few years, they want a company that looks like it'll be around.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for a banner, stale year or broken form. Note which.
openers.linkLine: Same deck and fence staining business, current and fast: {demo-link}

openers.line: On my phone, your deck gallery thumbnails are too small to see the grain. The grain is the whole sale for staining.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your deck staining gallery, sharp on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Getting a deck staining price from you means a call. Plenty of people would rather send the deck size, the railing count and the current colour, then hear back.
openers.hook: Check profile, listing and any site for a form. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A deck and fence quote form by size: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your before-and-afters of weathered grey decks brought back to warm wood are the best advert this trade has. They're scattered in the feed with nowhere to land.
openers.hook: Pick two transformations you could describe by wood and stain colour. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those deck restorations, side by side: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews say the deck still looks good a couple of summers later, no peeling. That's the fear every buyer has after a bad stain job, and it stays on Google.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about durability or prep. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Those deck staining reviews where buyers decide: {demo-link}

openers.line: Spring is when everyone uncovers the grill and notices the deck looks tired. The staining crews people can find in March book out the early summer.
openers.hook: Use from late winter to early spring. Name the month in the reply.

openers.line: Early fall is the last good stretch for staining before it gets cold. A page for fence staining slots catches people who missed the spring.
openers.hook: Use in late summer and early fall. Name the season.
openers.linkLine: Fall deck and fence staining slots: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a helper for the staining crew. People looking for steady outdoor work check how established a deck company looks first.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A deck staining page with careers: {demo-link}

openers.line: You stain decks across {City} and nearby, but nothing tells someone in {Neighborhood} you'll come. 'Deck staining' plus the town is what they type.
openers.hook: Find towns they mention in posts or reviews. Use the furthest.
openers.linkLine: A deck staining page for every town: {demo-link}

openers.line: Stain wears on a cycle, so every deck you've done will need you again. A restain plan sign-up turns those decks into spring bookings without a single call.
openers.hook: Look for reviews from repeat customers. Quote one back.

openers.line: Staining means chemicals near gardens and overspray near cars. A page showing your insurance and how you protect plants and neighbours' fences settles the worry.
openers.hook: Check whether they mention insurance anywhere. Never quote a policy you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and protection on one deck staining page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Fence builders tell every customer to stain the new cedar after it dries, and some of them send people your way. Those referrals still search your name.
openers.hook: Look for reviews mentioning a new fence or a builder's referral. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a fence builder's staining referral lands: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted has a rich, even stain and clean railings. A deck like that should be the first thing a visitor sees.
openers.hook: Pick their newest deck or fence and name it: wood, stain colour, and the street if tagged.
openers.linkLine: That deck staining job, front and centre: {demo-link}

objections.objection: Staining is seasonal, I can't justify a website.
objections.handler: "That's the case for it. The restain plan books your spring in winter, and the fall page fills the end of the season."

objections.objection: My work comes from fence builders and painters.
objections.handler: "Good partners. Their customers still search your name before calling, and the colour guide answers the questions they'd otherwise ask you on the phone."

objections.objection: People just want the cheapest stain job.
objections.handler: "Some do. The prep page is for the ones who've watched a cheap stain peel. Once they see the stripping and sanding, your price makes sense."

objections.objection: I already do most of my marketing in local groups.
objections.handler: "Keep doing it. Those posts send people to look you up, and now they'll find a quote form and a colour guide instead of a dead end."

objections.objection: My daughter can make me a site.
objections.handler: "Great, family's cheaper. Happy to pass along the colour guide layout. If it stalls before spring, the offer stands."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, for the colour guide, prep page, quote form and plan sign-up. About one deck."

bullets: Peg the build to one large deck and railing job, never an hourly rate.
The colour and opacity guide is the centrepiece; price it by the number of colours and woods shown.
Quote forms that ask deck size, railings, stairs and current finish are their own line.
The restain plan sign-up is where repeat revenue lives; price it separately.
Fence staining gets its own page and price line; it's searched and priced differently from decks.
Keep it lean; the business is seasonal and cash is tight in winter.
